points: "Zacharti lach chesed ne'urayich": before all the rebuke, Hashem says I remember your love when you followed Me into the desert. The rebuke is built on love.
The leaders failed: the Kohanim never taught people to ask "Ayeh Hashem?" Those who held the Torah knew its laws but didn't know Hashem. Yoshiyahu, the righteous king, isn't criticized.
When unnatural things happen to you, ask why Hashem is allowing it. It's a message to change. They committed the three cardinal sins: idolatry, adultery and murder.
Instead of changing, they argue with Yirmiyahu. Hashem doesn't demand we never make mistakes, only that we take responsibility and change.
The chesed in that pasuk is Hashem's: He gave us a hard test in the desert so we could prove our faith. A challenge can be a deeper kindness from Hashem.
